newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE COFFEE ENDS LOWER, LOOKS WEAK.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE COFFEE ENDS LOWER, LOOKS WEAK.

text.p: LIFFE coffee ended lower and looking weak after spot September dived through psychological support at $1,600, traders said.
By the close active September was $110 lower at $1,520, at a discount to November at $1,540. September volume was 3,200 of the total 6,533 lots.
It would be weak as long as September/November was at a discount, one said. "While it (the discount) remains, I can't see it changing," he said.
Brazil exported 916,598 60-kg bags of coffee, ground and in beans, in July, down from an adjusted June figure of 1.00 million bags, said Federation of Coffee Exporters (Febec).
Hawaii is expected to produce 6.4 million lbs of coffee in the 1996-97 season, the largest harvest in three decades, U.S. Agriculture Department said Tuesday.
